title: Enterprise ask - quick economic viability estimator and delivery-complexity proxy for Sales/CS triage
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Purpose: Create a lightweight estimator and playbook that Sales/CS can use during earliest customer conversations to classify enterprise feature requests by: (1) near-term economic viability (how likely this drives committed spend in 3-12 months) and (2) delivery complexity (rough engineering effort + infra risk). The goal is to reduce back-and-forth with PM/Eng and produce consistent initial scoping that enables faster commercial motion and better routing to Dedicated/Private requirements when relevant.

Why now: Field teams spend a lot of time collecting details from customers before we can provide a credible scope/econ read. This slows sales cycles and floods PM with low-signal asks. A quick proxy will streamline the intake funnel, prioritize high-value asks, and surface tech constraints early (e.g., data residency, model fine-tuning, dedicated capacity needs).

Outcomes expected:
- Standardized 5-question form and a 7-point rubric that outputs a two-axis score (EconScore 0-10, Complexity 0-10) and a routing recommendation (Quick Win / Needs Eng POC / Requires Dedicated/Private / Enterprise Program).
- One-page playbook for CS to interpret scores and next steps.
- Pilot with two enterprise AE squads and handoff guidance to PM/Eng/SE.

Scope: Lightweight (no full engineering discovery). The estimator is intentionally conservative — it should bias toward escalation when uncertain. The deliverables are a shared Google Sheet tool, an internal playbook doc (Confluence), and a short training slide deck for AEs and CSMs.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Shared estimator tool (Google Sheet) with automated EconScore and Complexity outputs and routing column.
2) Playbook doc in Confluence with definitions, examples, and sample answers for common Redwood asks (e.g., Dedicated pool request, private deployment, KMS integration, latency SLO adjustments, KV cache changes).
3) Two AE squads trained and using the tool in pilot for >= 4 live asks.
4) At least one escalation pattern defined (SE engagement, Dedicated scoping request, Legal/Risk flag).
5) PM feedback loop defined to convert top 20% of high-econ/low-complexity asks to scoped PRDs in 2 sprints.
success_metrics:
- Median time from initial CS intake to accepted first-scope note reduces from X days to <= 3 business days.
- % of pilot intakes with complete initial scope increases to >= 75%.
- Conversion rate of high EconScore/low Complexity asks to commercial commitments (pilot cohort) >= 30% within 3 months.
- Fewer one-off deep-dive meetings requested from PM/Eng for low-priority asks (target -40%).
proposed_solution:
1) Design a 5-question quick form (ARR proxy, user count & integration surface, regulatory/data residency need, model or infra changes required, timeframe/urgency). Each answer maps to numeric buckets used to compute EconScore and Complexity.
2) Complexity scoring includes explicit engineering flags: model changes (fine-tune/new weights), infra changes (DED/Private), SLO/latency risk, data pipeline work, security/compliance gating.
3) Provide an interpretive playbook: what to do for each routing category, escalation contacts (SE on-call, infra lead, legal), and templated follow-ups.
4) Build a one-tab Google Sheet that accepts inputs and shows color-coded routing + recommended next step. No internal app required for MVP.
5) Capture anonymized intake examples and a short FAQ for common edge cases.
steps:
1) Workshop with Sales leadership and two AE squads to validate form fields (week 0).
2) Build sheet prototype + Confluence playbook (week 1).
3) Run training session and capture feedback (week 2).
4) Pilot with 4-6 live asks, collect telemetry and qualitative notes (weeks 3-6).
5) Iterate rules and roll out org-wide if metrics meet thresholds (weeks 7-10).
open_questions: What ARR bands should map to immediate-high priority vs nurture?
Do we treat dedicated/private deployment requests with identical econ weighting as API-only feature asks?
Should we require a CSM/AE sign-off before escalation to Eng for requests flagged as high complexity?
Are there existing dashboards (Console) we can push intake metrics to for long-term tracking?
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Sales might over-score econ to get faster attention. Mitigation: conservative default mapping, PM spot-checks weekly.
Risk: Estimator misses compliance nuances. Mitigation: include explicit question and Legal quick-flag path.
Risk: AEs avoid using the tool if it adds friction. Mitigation: keep form to 5 fields and embed quick examples; instrument feedback button.
Risk: Engineering receives too many escalations. Mitigation: routing prioritizes Econ/Complexity intersection and caps weekly escalations per squad for pilot.
